THE ONE REJECTION IS A REAL AUTHORING DEFECT AND IT IS IN THE SHIPPED SET: CS10-07 option A claims the heat island effect is largest on overcast nights, which is backwards -- the nocturnal urban heat island is SUPPRESSED under cloud, not maximised -- and the option's own causal clause does not support it, since cloud traps outgoing heat over the rural reference site just as much as over the city. Recorded rather than repaired: it is one option in one item, the item is not thereby solvable (three options remain and the grader did not claim otherwise), and a rewrite round on a cleared batch is the pattern that has traded one defect for another three times this week. Named here so whoever touches CS10-07 next fixes that option rather than rediscovering it. THE GRADER DECLINED TO COUNT THREE NEAR-MISSES AND NAMED THEM SEPARATELY, which is the behaviour this stage needs: CS10-06's C and D are the intentional and the distributional form of one proposition, and CS10-18's A entails D. Both are UNIQUENESS RISKS FOR THE AUTHOR, not student-usable eliminations -- nothing tells a solver which member of the pair is the distractor. WHY THE BATCH SURVIVES, in the grader's words: 'opposed and permuted structures are structurally elimination-proof -- you cannot drop a direction without knowing which direction the passage went.' Several sets are outright opposed pairs or permutations. The other consistent property is that the option sets are DOMAIN-FAITHFUL IN ALL FOUR SLOTS: on CS10-11 all four are real published single-photoreceptor colour-vision mechanisms, and B reads implausible enough on its face to invite exactly the unfounded rejection this stage exists to catch -- it survives.

nosource.verdict: FAILED AS A BATCH AND THE MATCHED CONTROL CONFIRMS IT. Cause, named identically by all three solvers: the option set RECONSTRUCTS THE HIDDEN STEM. Three or four choices drawn from one polysemous word's other sense-family (flag, arrest, check, wax, bearing, court, canvass) plus an orthographic look-alike name the stem, and the one remaining word is the key. That is the PUBLISHED distractor doctrine - 'a word from the stem's other meaning', 'a look-alike' - applied faithfully; it makes an item hard WITH the stem and trivial WITHOUT it. KEPT SET CAVEAT, stated because the number would otherwise be read as a measurement: the 18 kept are those the blind panel failed to solve, so their residual (14.8) is SELECTED ON THE OUTCOME and is not an independent estimate. They are kept because each also passed the with-source grade, not because that residual clears anything.

nosource.verdict: THE CORRECTED BRIEF WORKED, MEASURED AGAINST THE SAME FLOOR THAT CONDEMNED ITS PREDECESSOR. A NEW cross-item tell was found here and is the reason 8 items were dropped: all three solvers independently reported that the cohort reuses a small filler pool (400 slots, 314 distinct words; 'hollow' in 8 sets), so an option unique to the cohort is almost certainly the key. Measured exactly: 11 items have exactly one cohort-unique option and it is the key in 8, 72.7% against a 20.0% control. The live bank recycles MORE (1.48 uses per word vs 1.27) and the tell never fires there, because its recycling is whole-pool via bijective sets and leaves nothing unique - partial recycling that leaves one outlier is the defect, heavy recycling is not.

tells.verdict: BATCH-LEVEL tell, found by a grader and acted on, that neither the blind attack nor any per-item check could see: 12 of 17 survivors closed on the same X-not-Y contrastive frame, and SIX shared one semantic relation - the record measures its own production process, not its subject (WIC3-01, -05, -08, -12, -19, -20). Because Craft and Structure is the BINDING domain these items would be drawn into one form together, so a student could learn the spec instead of the vocabulary. Cut to three of the six (08, 12, 19) on the grader's own recommendation. Shipping key letters A3/B3/C3/D1 over 10, max 3, no complete permutation window.

batches.note: 39 of 42 authored survive. Commissioned across five domains at once because ACT math needs all five to buy form 14 -- a single-domain batch there once bought zero forms. My brief said the section is FIVE-choice; it is four under the enhanced ACT, and the author overruled me from act-test.ts and a 580/580 four-choice live bank. My brief also asked for 4 Statistics and Probability items where 5 are needed, so that domain remains short and is commissioned separately.

shape.verdict: 42 authored, all exactly 4 choices, key present among the choices, no duplicate option values within an item, no duplicate ids, no explanation naming a slot letter. Sandbox: 42/42 keys recompute and 126/126 distractors recompute to their named derivation. The author break-tested that harness by promoting every one of the 126 distractors to key -- all 126 refused -- and then attacked the harness itself with a rigged mutant whose solve really returns the promoted option, which was reported OK, so the refusals are a measurement rather than a harness that fails everything.

withsource.verdict: An independent grader solved all 42 from the prompt before reading any explanation and re-checked the fiddly ones with its own script: ALL 42 KEYS CORRECT, zero disputed. It found three real defects and all three are dropped. AM11S-04: the distractor "12" is the INCLUSIVE quartile convention (Excel QUARTILE.INC), so it is the answer a correctly-taught student gives, not an error -- a second defensible answer, which this project treats as broken. AM11A-07 and AM11F-09 share a malformed template ("For how large an integer k does the equation...", "How small an angle theta... satisfies...") that is not a well-formed question; two items from one bad template is a brief problem, not two authoring slips. Difficulty is banked from the GRADER, not the author: easy 4 / medium 33 / hard 2 against the author's 2/33/7. The grader demoted five of the seven "hard" labels, which matches this project's standing finding that authors over-label hard. Distractors 28 strong / 14 plausible / 0 weak.

nosource.verdict: Options-only attack, three solvers, interleaved with a composition-matched live control of 42 shipped ACT math items, arm recorded only in the key. CANDIDATE 29.4% against a derived best-fixed-letter control of 35.7%, margin -6.3; CONTROL 28.6% against 28.6%, margin 0.0. Zero items were reported solvable from the option set by the with-source grader. 38 items were byte-identical across the pre- and post-repair files so their answers are reused; the 4 items whose option sets changed were re-attacked fresh in a second render and merged.

tells.verdict: THE TELL THE POOLED MARGIN COULD NOT SEE, found and repaired. The key was the largest of four options on 7.1% of items against 21.4% in the live bank (z = -2.25) -- a free "eliminate the largest" worth 1/4 -> 1/3, and the solver applying it mechanically scored exactly 33.3%. A pooled margin cannot detect this because the derived control rises with the tell. Repaired on the author's own terms, never by inventing a pathless distractor: 4 items changed, each new distractor carrying a named wrong path (an altitude attached to the wrong side, a rectangle's diagonals assumed perpendicular, a rate misread as per-100-feet, the upper-half spread reported as the IQR). After repair and drops: largest 15.4% (z = -0.92), smallest 20.5% (z = -0.42), consistent with the live bank. check-key-magnitude.mjs is self-tested on 11 fixtures and break-tests correctly against the pre-repair file. Numeric hub key-is-hub 0.0%; key-is-sum 0.0%; no two options share a value.

withsource.verdict: An independent grader solved all 34 from the prompts by hand before reading any explanation, then re-solved them in a script written from the prompts rather than from the authors' solve fields. NO KEY DISPUTED, none second-defensible, no malformed stem. It brute-forced the two most error-prone items over their coefficient space rather than following the author's algebra. Seven items dropped: SM12L-12 and SM12L-20 graded distractor_quality "weak" (20 is effectively a two-option item -- 7/3 dies on the word "integer" and 12 is nowhere near the algebra); SM12L-03 because option 7's stated wrong path is incoherent, altering the wrong side of the equation and yielding a non-arithmetic sequence, so the option does no work; SM12L-17 and SM12A-14 as near-duplicates of SM12L-02 and SM12A-02 (one skill and one recalled fact respectively); plus the two repair regressions below. Difficulty banked from the GRADER: easy 8 / medium 11 / hard 8, against the author's 12 hard.

nosource.verdict: Options-only attack, three solvers, interleaved with a composition-matched live control of 34 shipped SAT math items, arm recorded only in the key. CANDIDATE 36.3% against a derived best-fixed-letter control of 32.4%, margin +3.9; CONTROL 35.3% against 32.4%, margin +2.9 -- the two arms are indistinguishable. Solvers' own confident picks scored BELOW chance: one solver's ten "mechanism" calls came in at 10.0%. No solver could reconstruct a question from an option set. The attack was re-run in full at this content hash rather than reusing the pre-repair run.

tells.verdict: INTERIOR BIAS FOUND AND REPAIRED, AND THE REPAIR INTRODUCED A NEW TELL THAT THE GRADER THEN CAUGHT. The key sat at an interior rank on 85.3% of items against 68.4% live (z = +2.12) -- "eliminate both extremes" was worth about 8 points. Repaired to 67.6% by changing six items, each deleting one option and adding one on the other side of the key with a named wrong path. THEN: the fix to SM12A-16 left its set as {1, 2, 1/2, 3}, making the key the ONLY non-integer -- answerable without solving, and invisible to the letter-spread check, the magnitude check and the blind attack alike. SM12L-14's new option 21 was the literal total printed in its own stem. Both are dropped rather than re-repaired, per the rule that after one failed rewrite you stop. Final kept set: largest 18.5%, smallest 11.1%, interior 70.4%, all within z = 0.74 of live. NOTE the checker itself was fixed during this batch -- it measured largest and smallest as separate marginals and PASSED the pre-repair file at exit 0; interior is now part of its verdict and it now fails that file at z = +2.12.

Sandbox: 6/6 keys recompute, 18/18 distractors recompute to their named derivation. The author break-tested that harness two ways on a copy -- mis-keying an item dropped the sandbox to 5/6, and corrupting a distractor derivation produced a mismatch -- so the green is a check that would have failed.

withsource.verdict: An independent grader solved all six from the prompts before reading any explanation: ALL SIX KEYS CORRECT, none second-defensible, no duplicate ideas, no malformed stems, no option colliding with a numeral in its own stem. It specifically cleared the two convention risks: AM11T-06's overlap is forced to exactly 2 by "every student plays at least one", and AM11T-01's median is 2 under every convention because positions 10 and 11 are both 2 -- the structural opposite of the inclusive-quartile item dropped from the previous batch. Difficulty banked from the grader: easy 2 / medium 4 / hard 0 against the author's 1/4/1; the author had already declined to defend its own "hard" label. Two items dropped on this grader's findings: AM11T-01's "7" distractor is DEAD (a frequency outside the 0-4 range every stem value occupies, making the item three-choice), and AM11T-06's distractors are weak enough that it is close to two-option.

nosource.verdict: Options-only attack, three solvers, 6 candidate items interleaved with 18 composition-matched live Statistics and Probability items, arm only in the key. CANDIDATE 27.8% against a derived control of 33.3% (margin -5.6); CONTROL 27.8% against 27.8% (margin 0.0). READ THE DENOMINATOR: n=6 cannot support a rate, so the per-item result is what decides. Exactly one candidate item was solved by all three solvers -- AM11T-04 -- and two solvers independently named the same mechanism: its option set carries the complete with/without-replacement family ((4/12)^2, (4/12)(4/11), (4/12)(3/11)), so the distractors announce the stem. It is dropped. None of the three kept items was solved by more than one solver. NOTE ON THE DEAL: a free per-item shuffle dealt five of six keys to one letter, giving a best-fixed-letter control of 83.3% and making the arm unmeasurable; rather than re-roll seeds until the deal looked fair, the key SLOT was dealt as evenly as the count allows (precedent: the ssat-cofounder sitting dealt 40 items flat for a control of exactly 20.0%).

tells.verdict: check-key-magnitude REFUSES at n<10, correctly, so the batch was measured pooled with the 42-item v11 batch it supplements: largest 16.7%, smallest 18.8%, interior 64.6% against a live 21.0/23.1/55.9, all within z=1.22. The 6 alone deal one key largest and one smallest by construction. Numeric hub: no derivational structure in any option set. A leak specific to this domain was found and is recorded for the brief: where an author computes distractors from one two-way table, the joint, the marginal and the reverse conditional appear as siblings and that family is a fingerprint of the stem -- a solver reconstructed AM11T-02's question from its option set alone, though it could not answer it (0 of 3). Statistics option sets leak more than bare algebra ones.

withsource.verdict: An independent grader solved all five from the prompts before reading explanations, then re-verified by exhaustive scan including a rational-grid sweep for the absolute-value item and a full piecewise scan for the cost item. NO KEY DISPUTED, none second-defensible, no stem-value collision, every distractor path coherent. It checked the two boundary conventions explicitly rather than by sweep: SM13L-03's limit is stated twice in agreeing phrasings and neither candidate lands ON the bound, so no strict-vs-inclusive reading rescues 17; SM13L-05 has A and B EXACTLY equal at n=20, so 20 is a strong trap rather than a competing-convention second key. Difficulty from the grader: 2 easy / 2 medium / 1 hard against the author's 1/2/2. Two dropped on its findings -- SM13L-01 carries a dead option (210 exceeds the time to drain the whole tank) making it three-choice, and SM13L-02 is easy with an incoherent 190 distractor that divides on the wrong side yet handles 3z correctly.

nosource.verdict: Options-only attack, three solvers, 5 candidates interleaved with 15 composition-matched live Algebra items, arm only in the key, key SLOT dealt flat because n=5 cannot carry a free shuffle. CANDIDATE 33.3% against a derived control of 40.0% (margin -6.7); CONTROL 17.8% against 26.7% (margin -8.9). Both below their own controls. READ THE DENOMINATOR: n=5 cannot support a rate, so the per-item result decides. SM13L-04 was solved by ALL THREE solvers and is dropped -- it was the with-source grader's top pick, the only genuinely hard item with the strongest distractor set, and the unanimous blind solve outranks that. ALL FIVE of the solvers' self-labelled "mechanism" picks across the whole render were WRONG, which is the third maths batch running where confident structural reasoning scores below chance.

tells.verdict: check-key-magnitude refuses at n<10, so the batch was measured pooled with sat-math-v12.kept: largest 18.8%, smallest 12.5%, interior 68.8% against live 15.3/16.3/68.5 -- z = 0.55 / -0.58 / 0.03, the closest match to the live distribution of any batch this session. ONE RESIDUAL RECORDED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: the two survivors share a mechanism. Both SM13L-03 and SM13L-05 are one-variable inequalities whose answer is the integer at a boundary, with the off-by-one in the option list; the grader named the collision and recommended shipping 04 and 05, which the blind half then vetoed. Different surfaces (a weight budget against a two-tier price) and strong distractors on both, but Algebra is the BINDING domain so new items are drawn together -- if a third Algebra item is authored, it must not be a boundary item.
